article.title: Git Hook Topology
article.subtitle: Singine-managed hook relationships across the main working repositories
article.para: This topic documents the current shared hook model for the active Sindoc repositories. The hooks themselves are thin launchers. They delegate to Singine, and Singine decides what follow-up command to run for the current repository and event.

sidebar.para: Lists the registered repositories and their declared archetypes.
Installs the shared pre-commit, post-commit, and post-merge launchers into every registered repository.
Renders the current topology in Mermaid form from the same registry.

listitem.para: Git fires a local hook such as pre-commit or post-merge.
The installed hook launcher calls python3 -m singine.command git hooks run --event ... --repo-root ....
Singine resolves the repository from its registry and runs the commands configured for that event.
The repository-specific command completes, and its output becomes the local hook feedback.

sidebar.para: pre-commit delegates to singine git hooks run --event pre-commit --repo-root /Users/skh/ws/git/github/sindoc/datatech-wiki-kg, which runs python3 scripts/check_wikipedia_quality.py.
post-commit and post-merge delegate to the same Singine surface and run python3 scripts/refresh_repo.py.
pre-commit delegates to singine git hooks run --event pre-commit --repo-root /Users/skh/ws/git/github/sindoc/singine, which runs python3 -m py_compile singine/command.py singine/wikipedia_contrib.py.
post-commit and post-merge currently remain registry-backed no-op surfaces so the same control model applies without forcing a heavyweight local pipeline.
The installed hooks call the Singine runner and currently serve as registry-backed no-op surfaces until a SilkPage-specific verification or rendering command is promoted into the shared registry.
